summary: Canonical diagnostic solutions and publication lifecycle

delivery.outcome: Ticket allocation and publication stay collision-free and state-correct, while every stable governance diagnostic has one canonical machine remediation and optional structured human runbook
nonGoals: No migration or deletion of historical ticket evidence
No automatic cleanup or mutation by diagnostic checkers
No weakening of fail-closed governance gates
No completion or publication of ticket-065

architecture.decision: Keep rules normative, register each stable code and short remediation in diagnostics.json, store only multi-step human procedures under error/, and detect clone-local allocation bypasses in the read-only workspace audit
interfaceChanges: C-PUBLISH-003 remains in PUBLICATION until trusted merge
diagnostics catalog changes to structured v2 entries
adopted package exposes structured error runbooks
dataChanges: diagnostics.json stores message, remediation and optional documentation per code
architecture.rollback: Revert before merge; do not restore manual allocation or premature DONE transitions after publication

validation.evidence: Fixtures distinguish reserved tickets from unreserved filesystem claims and divergent same-number intents
Publication rule fragments and rule mapping reject the premature DONE transition
All emitted GOV codes are catalogued and linked runbooks are structurally valid and installed

commands: all commands from the Linux CI test job
validation.evidence: Focused and complete contracts retain the baseline
